Parem uses this only to lock the screen when its accessibility service can\'t. After each such lock, your next unlock needs your PIN, pattern or password: fingerprint and face unlock won\'t work for it. Parem uses no other device admin power, and locking reads and sends nothing. To uninstall Parem, first turn this off in Parem\'s Settings › Gestures.

Parem saved a report of the crash on this phone. Parem has sent nothing. Send opens an app you choose with the full report, so you can read it before it goes anywhere. It holds the error, which can name an app or a web address, plus Parem\'s version, the Android version, the phone\'s maker and model, and the time. It includes no app list, contacts or settings.

Parem counts screen time through Android\'s usage access: the total on the home screen, app limits, sort by usage and the weekly graph all depend on it. \n\nCounted on this phone. Parem sends these numbers nowhere and keeps them out of Android cloud backup. A phone-to-phone transfer you start can copy them to your new phone.

Double tap to lock uses Android\'s accessibility service. Android tells Parem\'s service when you tap inside Parem. The service ignores every tap except the one on its own invisible lock area, and when that tap comes it asks Android to lock the screen. It gets no events from other apps and cannot read your screen. Nothing it sees is stored or sent anywhere. You can turn it off any time in Accessibility settings.

Parem\'s accessibility service is no longer running, so your lock gesture cannot lock the screen. Android can turn it off after an app update, a crash, or when a security setting restricts accessibility services. Turn it back on in Accessibility settings, or pick another gesture action in Parem\'s gesture settings.

Eligible notifications from apps you have not allowed can move to a quiet list. Choose a swipe gesture in Parem settings to open it from home.

Parem excludes some system apps and categories, including notifications identified as calls, alarms, media, navigation or system alerts. Apps may label notifications differently.

A sound or vibration may still occur when a notification arrives. From Parem you can open Android notification settings for an app; if you make its notifications silent, they may stay in the shade instead of the quiet list.

Parem reads each notification’s app and type on this device to sort it, and shows its title in the quiet list. For hidden items, it stores a technical key and the snooze time, and the notification’s timestamp if you open or dismiss it. The key can include a tag chosen by the app. Parem does not separately store the notification title or body or send this data.

Parem asks Android to snooze eligible notifications for 8 hours and may hide them again while the filter is on. When you turn the filter off, Parem tries to release items it can reach; some may stay snoozed until their snooze ends. You can also remove access in Android Settings › Notification access.

App limits need usage access: Parem counts how long each app is open. Without it a limit can never fire.\n\nCounted on this phone. Parem sends these numbers nowhere and keeps them out of Android cloud backup. A phone-to-phone transfer you start can copy them to your new phone.
Parem counts screen time with it: the total on the home screen, app limits, sort by usage and the weekly graph. Turning it off in Android turns all of those off.

Double-tap empty home space to lock your phone

Double-tap empty space on your home screen to lock your phone. Change the action in Settings › Gestures. To remove accessibility access, use Android Settings › Accessibility. If device admin is your lock method, turn it off in Parem’s gesture settings.

Mindful pause asks why you are opening an app, then waits five seconds before you can open it. Tap an app’s limit and choose Pause only, or set a time limit and turn the pause on from the same list.\n\nThe list shows apps used today, and Add another app reaches the rest. You can also long-press an app on home and choose its time-limit action. Limits show a warning you can override; they do not permanently block an app.
No usage is available yet. Finish setup, add an app to home, then long-press it and choose Time limit. Or open Settings › Calm › App limits after using an app.

Swipe up on home for all apps. Long-press empty home space for the home menu, including Settings and Add widget. Swipe down opens notifications by default; change it in Settings › Gestures.

Long-press an empty app slot to choose an app. Long-press an occupied slot to change or remove it, create a folder, or add a website shortcut. Tap a folder to choose one of its apps; websites open in your browser. Settings › Home screen controls the number of slots, alignment and layout lock. Layout lock prevents edits through the slot long-press menu.

Tap the clock or date to open Clock or Calendar; long-press to choose another app. Tap the screen-time total for its graph.

Add widgets from the home menu. Drag the handle at a widget’s bottom edge to resize it. Hold the widget to swap, move or remove it. Settings controls whether widgets sit above or below apps; wide tablet layouts place them beside the home content.

Swipe up, then type an app name. Fuzzy matching lets you use parts of the name. Auto show keyboard in Settings › Search controls whether typing is ready when the drawer opens. Press Back to return home. A single matching app opens automatically by default. Turn off Open single match automatically in Settings › Search if you prefer to tap or press Enter. Automatic opening is off with a screen reader.

Long-press an app in the drawer for its available actions, such as hiding it, app info or uninstalling. Use Rename in the app menu to change its label. Find hidden apps again under Hidden apps in Settings, which also shows how many there are. Hiding an app does not uninstall it. With usage access, you can sort the drawer by use and see app open counts.

Contact search is optional in Settings › Search. It asks for Contacts access and matches names to phone numbers on your device; choosing a match opens the dialer. Search history is optional in the same section. Recent searches stay on this phone, can be cleared there, and are erased when history is switched off.

Work-profile apps are badged where Android makes them available. On supported Android versions, the drawer’s Private space row lets you lock or unlock that space. Search for “private” or “private space” to reach it without scrolling. Tap the result or press Enter to unlock or open it. Its apps are hidden while it is locked. If you hide the space when locked in Android settings, its entry also stays out of the drawer and search; reveal it through Android Settings › Security & privacy › Private space. Work-profile widgets appear in the widget picker when available.

The app drawer search field also accepts tools. Try 2+2, 5 km to mi, or 100 eur in usd. Tap a calculation or conversion result to copy it, or press Enter. Currency conversion downloads European Central Bank rates when needed; the result shows their date and needs an internet connection for new rates.

Type a phone number to open it in the dialer. Start a query with a space to search Google, or use a DuckDuckGo bang such as !w calm. Web searches open your browser.

Try alarm 7:30, timer 10m, or event friday 3pm dentist. Parem passes the action to a compatible Clock or Calendar app. Supported action words include English and Estonian.

Type a setting name, such as grayscale, to jump to its row in Settings. App shortcut words, such as incog, can find actions published by installed apps. Shortcuts depend on what each app provides and do not replace a single matching app’s automatic launch.

Settings › Gestures lets you change left and right swipes, swipe down and double tap. Available actions include an app, search, notifications, lock, camera or flashlight; the quiet-list action appears when its filter is enabled. Choose None to turn a swipe off.

Turn on Gesture letters in Settings › Gestures and assign apps to letters. Draw the letter in one continuous stroke on home. Straight strokes remain swipes. Recognition depends on the letter shape; lift your finger to finish.

With a hardware keyboard, typing on home opens app search; the Menu key opens the drawer. Use the D-pad and Enter to choose an app, or hold Enter for its menu. TalkBack offers home actions and a visible All apps row, so gestures are optional.

Usage access lets Parem count time spent in apps on this phone. Tap the home screen-time total for daily app usage, the seven-day graph and a weekly comparison when enough history exists. Manage access in Settings › Calm.

App limits warn when you have used an app for its daily allowance. Open anyway overrides the warning. Add a limit from an app’s home menu or the App limits sheet. That sheet lists the most-used apps from today. Add another app reaches everything else. Choose Pause only for a five-second wait before launches, with a prompt to consider why you are opening the app, and no time limit. With a limit set, long-press the app again and turn on Mindful pause, or reopen its limit picker in the App limits sheet. No limit removes both.

Focus mode blocks Parem launches except your allowed apps and calls. Choose a timed session or weekly windows in Settings › Calm › Focus mode. Windows can cross midnight; matching start and end times mean all day. Disable pauses a currently active scheduled window until that run ends.

Limits, pause and focus guard launches through Parem. They do not close an app already open or prevent Android and other apps from opening it. Websites and search quick actions are not app launches guarded by these limits.

Quiet notifications can move eligible notifications from apps outside your allowed list out of the shade. Some categories and system apps are excluded, but apps can label notifications differently. A sound or vibration may still happen. Make silent opens Android notification settings; silent notifications may remain in the shade. Choose a swipe in Parem settings to open the quiet list. When you turn the filter off, Parem tries to release reachable items; some may remain snoozed until their snooze ends. Setup explains notification access before you grant it.

Grayscale removes color from the screen. It needs a one-time developer-tools permission, and setup explains each step. After setup, choose Now, During focus or After a limit. Per-app grayscale is also available in app menus and needs usage access and Parem as default home. Color can always be restored in Android Settings › Accessibility › Color correction.

Double tap to lock uses Android’s accessibility service after your consent; it cannot read your screen. The alternative device-admin lock method is in Settings › Gestures and requires your PIN after each lock. You can change or disable the gesture there.

Settings › Appearance has light, dark and system themes, theme schedules, relative text size, bold font, daily wallpaper and status-bar visibility. Choose scheduled light and dark times, or sunrise and sunset. Choose a city for weather in Settings › Home screen. Text also follows Android’s font size.

Settings › Home screen controls app icons and icon packs, clock and date visibility, alignment and widget placement. Install a compatible icon pack first, then choose it through the icon setting.

Parem reduces motion when Android animations are off. Screen-reader and keyboard alternatives are available for core home actions.

Settings has Export settings and Import settings for moving your preferences. Android cloud backup leaves Parem out, so export before you move to a new phone. Import replaces saved preferences; export first if you want to keep a copy. Widgets and other device-specific grants are not transferred: add widgets and grant access again on the new phone. Search history is not exported.

Crash reports are off by default. If enabled, a report stays on this phone until you choose to share it after a crash. You can read it before sending or discard it. Reports include error details and device information.

App usage, contact matching and notification filtering happen on this phone. Features that need online data, such as weather, currency rates and daily wallpaper, make network requests; web searches and links go to the browser or another app you choose.

Your apps stay installed when you switch launchers. Use Parem’s default-launcher setting or Android Settings › Apps › Default apps › Home app to choose your previous home screen. Setting names vary by phone. All optional setup can be changed later in Settings.
